content_units: You have   9 hours 15 minutes of study time   before the quiz on   2026-11-08  :
1.   Center and spread  : mean, median, mode, standard deviation
Week   Dates   Focus   Key Sessions   Goal/Quiz

Day 1   2026-11-06 18:30-21:30 (UTC+1)   Build core foundations   18:30-19:15 mean/median/mode; 19:15-20:00 standard deviation; 20:00-20:45 break; 20:45-21:30 basic probability   Finish formulas/concepts once; solve 10-15 short questions accurately

Day 2   2026-11-07 09:00-16:00 (UTC+1)   Apply, connect, and rehearse   09:00-10:15 normal distribution; 10:15-11:15 z-scores; 11:15-12:00 scatterplots; 12:00-12:45 mixed practice; 12:45-13:30 break; 13:30-14:30 timed quiz set 1; 14:30-15:15 error review; 15:15-16:00 timed quiz set 2 + formula recap   Reach quiz-ready speed; identify and fix weak spots before test day
- Learn what each measure describes and when each is most useful.
- Focus question:   Which measure changes most when an outlier appears?
- Review spread and why standard deviation measures typical distance from the mean.
- Do 3-5 hand-worked examples with simple numbers.
- Learn the interpretation, even if your class uses calculator-based computation:
- high SD = values more spread out
- End by writing 4 rules from memory.
- Learn the bell-curve idea: center, spread, symmetry.
- Connect normal distribution to mean and standard deviation.
- what percent is above/below a value conceptually
- find z from a raw score
- compare two scores with different scales
- Practice with 5-6 plots or textbook-style questions.
- For each graph, answer in one sentence:
- Do one short set covering all topics.
- Aim for method clarity, not speed.
- No notes unless your real quiz allows them.
- Split questions roughly across all six topics.
- Rework every missed or guessed problem.
- For each error, note the reason:
- Redo at least 2 questions of the same type.
- Do a shorter second round with emphasis on weak areas.
- summarize each topic aloud in 1-2 lines
Final Review Checklist for 2026-11-07 Evening or 2026-11-08 Morning
- I can compute   mean, median, and mode   and know when each is preferable.
- I can explain what   standard deviation   tells me about spread.
- I can solve basic   probability   questions, including complements and simple independent events.
- I understand the   normal distribution   as symmetric and centered at the mean.
- I can calculate and interpret a   z-score  .
- I can read a   scatterplot   for direction, strength, form, and outliers.
- I know which formulas or definitions I must remember without help.
- I have redone my weakest 5-10 questions correctly.
